review: Read three complete production modules and three tests, plus omitted synthetic local-connection fixture. First-party source and synthetic identifiers only; no live pairing IDs, invitation secrets, profiles or private history exported.

Durable pairing retains owner/chat-scoped review metadata and exact request identity. Unknown writes reconcile the same request. Automatic recovery reads never issue consent or new invitations. Fresh registration resets approval; account/chat changes unmount prior operations.

Accepted pairing, live runtime binding and task registration are separate states. Runtime matching checks pairing/profile/chat/run/expiry. Replacement and cancellation retain prior reviewed metadata until a verified server result permits transition; local deadlines alone cannot prove grant expiry.

Private MCP delivery is the default for a fresh review. Existing manual consent is preserved. Invitation secrets remain transient; secret-free setup requests are separate from manual claim handles. Explicit revocation has a separate confirmation.

Local personal-tool inspection is separately feature-gated and read-only. Identical valid tunnel notifications preserve its observation, changed/malformed events invalidate it, and deadline/late-result checks prevent stale display. It neither starts a tunnel nor grants a clock/program action.
No canonical source edits in this cohort. Export transformation is line endings only.
limits: Private source proposal only; not frozen, committed, pushed or newly packaged.
Mock tests do not establish owner consent, live account/device identity, installed MCP availability or game authority.
Shared schemas, local-connection fixture, native bridge, storage helpers and other imports remain separate dependencies.
Registration and historical success are observations, not active grant authority.
